en: Salt farmers in Dasol, Pangasinan, use solar evaporation to separate solid salt from liquid seawater.
A bowl of halo-halo is a heterogeneous mixture because you can easily see and separate its solid ingredients like ube halaya and saba.
Fermenting coconut sap into Ilocano vinegar is a chemical change that produces a completely new sour-tasting liquid.
Cold sago't gulaman causes water vapor in the humid Manila air to condense into liquid droplets on the glass.
The iron body of a jeepney undergoes a chemical change called rusting when exposed to the salty air of Manila Bay.
Baking powder releases carbon dioxide gas when heated, causing the Filipino steamed rice cake called puto to rise.
Builders use bamboo for bahay kubo walls because it is a natural thermal insulator that keeps the house cool.
The black sand beaches of Cagayan contain magnetite, a magnetic material that can be separated from non-magnetic sand using a magnet.
Solid tablea chocolate melts into a liquid when stirred into hot water to make the traditional Filipino drink called sikwate.
Strained salabat ginger tea with dissolved sugar is a homogeneous solution where the flavor is evenly distributed.
Freezing liquid buko juice in molds turns it into solid buko ice candy through a physical change of state.
Burning dried coconut leaves to cook adobo is a chemical change that produces heat, light, and ash.
